newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soy harvest lags average, yields near normal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soy harvest lags average, yields near normal.

text.p: Soybean harvest in key U.S. Midwest growing regions lagged average pace and yields were coming in near to slightly below normal levels, several grain merchandisers said.

"We're seeing yields mostly in the mid-40s to mid-50s (bushels per acre)," said Fred Gent, grain manager at McLean County Service Co in Bloomington, Ill. "I don't think we expected quite that good but that's about average for us."
Illinios' soybean harvest was 34 percent complete as of Sunday, well behind average pace of 73 percent.
USDA pegged Illinois soybean output at 39.0 bushels per acre (bpa), according to the October 11 crop report.
Most of the harvest delays were in northern Illinois where cool weather slowed development, Gent said, noting that combining was 65 to 70 percent complete near Bloomington.
Moisture levels were coming in at about 11 to 12 percent after several days of warm, windy weather aided evaporation, he said.
In Iowa, soybean harvest was 59 percent complete, compared with 63 percent for the five-year average.
Some central Iowa locations reported harvest was about 95 percent complete and yields were averaging 44 to 45 bpa, said Ron Gates, grain division manager for Heart of Iowa Co-op.
"We had some early planted beans that were better than that but then we got into those late planted ones where (summer) rains washed out big patches," Gates said.
"This week, if the weather holds off, we'll be essentially done (harvesting)," he added. "We're probably (yielding) 10 percent less than what we had a year ago at this time."
He said moisture levels were averaging 10 to 11 percent.
USDA estimated Iowa's soybean yield at 44.0 bpa, compared with 27 bpa last year.

In Indiana, soybean harvest was 27 percent complete as of Sunday, against 68 percent for the five-year average, the state Agricultural Statistics Service said. Average moisture content of harvested soybeans was reported at 14 percent.
USDA's estimate for Indiana soybean production was 38.0 bpa, according to the October 11 report.
In Minnesota, soybean harvest was 81 percent complete, compared with the five-year average of 53 percent. Moisture content was averaging 12 percent, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
USDA pegged Minnesota's soybean yield at 37.0 bpa.
